You use the active voice when you want the ‘doer' of the action to be the subject.
Example: Roger hit the ball with the bat.
You use the passive voice when you want the ‘receiver' of the action to be the subject.
Example: The ball was hit by Roger.

Most of spoken English uses active speech. In active sentences, the subject is the focus of the sentence.
Example:
Active sentence: Lorena finished the project.
Passive sentence: The project was finished by Lorena.

A passive sentence puts the emphasis on the object of the active sentence. It now becomes the subject and focus of the passive sentence.
It is not always necessary to mention the object in a passive sentence.
Example:
The old theater was redecorated.

You make the passive form of a verb by using tenses of the be verb followed by the past participle.
Example:
Active sentence: My son broke the vase.
Passive sentence: The vase was broken by my son.

Passive of Modal Verbs in the Present
You use the Simple Present passive form of modal verbs to put the emphasis on the receiver of the action.

As for other verbs, the Simple Present passive form of modal verbs puts the emphasis on the receiver of the action and not on the doer of the action.
Passive modal forms are often impersonal and do not require an object.
Example:
  • Sports shoes must be worn on the field.
  • Baseball may be played on Tuesdays.

Where is the "home of baseball"? Most baseball aficionados will probably tell you it's in Cooperstown, New York.
Cooperstown is a small village that has less than 3,000 residents. It was erroneously believed to be the place where the modern game of baseball was invented.
Today Cooperstown is the home of the Baseball Hall of Fame, a museum that pays tribute to the legends of baseball. The hall of fame was founded in 1939, and players like Ty Cobb and Babe Ruth were enshrined in the inaugural class.

To be eligible for the Hall of Fame, certain criteria must be met. First, the player must have been retired for at least five years. A managerial or advisory position can be held, but the candidate cannot be an active player. Next, ballots must be cast by the Baseball Writers' Association. Finally, the player may be voted in if they are included on at least 75% of the ballots. No player has ever been included on 100% of ballots, but legendary pitcher Tom Seaver came the closest. He was elected with 99% of the vote.
During the summer months, the number of patrons visiting the museum each day can be greater than the number of people who live in Cooperstown!

The museum has the greatest baseball collection in the world, including uniforms, photographs, and other memorabilia from the most famous teams and players.
It is also a source of information for serious baseball fans. Fans can learn the history of the sport and see the records of their favorite teams. For baseball lovers, the museum is a dream come true.

Dear Debs,
You were wrong and I was right. This tour is totally worthwhile, although I must admit that the countryside is a bit monotonous. (They say it's much more interesting around Marrakech, but we aren't going there until next week.)

Each of the seven cities that we toured is surprisingly different, but I'm writing particularly to tell you about our visit to Casablanca. As I write this, I am sitting in a café next to the mosque you see on the back of this card.

You know that I love visiting mosques, and this one is particularly special. This gorgeous structure was named after the late king. It has a main prayer-hall about 650 feet long and 325 feet wide and can hold 25,000 (yes, 25,000!) people. Every inch of floor, wall, and ceiling is beautiful beyond words.

I took three rolls of pictures so that when I come home you'll be able to see all the details! Steven is even taking a picture of me now, writing you this card! Until then, take care and don't work too hard.

Good morning and welcome to The Gourmet Chef radio show. This morning, our show will focus on how to make a variety of delicious soups to impress your guests. Let's begin with a simple vegetarian soup stock.

To begin, take two white onions, two celery stalks, and two carrots. Chop them into 1-2 inch sized pieces. I think the secret of really great soup is in the choice of ingredients. But what you do with the ingredients is also very important. Take this celery, for example. If you chop the slices too small, they'll dissolve. But you don't want the celery pieces to be too large, either.

Next, heat a teaspoon of oil in a large pot. Add the chopped vegetables with a teaspoon of pepper and a teaspoon of salt. Now add seven strands of parsley leaves, two bay leaves, and 6-8 cups of water. Bring to a boil and then reduce the heat to low. It smells delicious already, doesn't it? Let it cook for an hour, then gently strain the soup stock from the vegetables.
Here we have the final product. Try some. Tastes wonderful, doesn't it?
